title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: OHLviz creates consistent, customizable charts Ontario Hockey League data. plotting functions accept data frames return ggplot objects. OHLpkg handles data retrieval, preparation, filtering, analysis. OHLviz handles visualization. can also use data sources specifying column names.
code: library(OHLviz)

title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: Supply one season consistent reporting scope per chart. Apply qualification filters plotting, resolve duplicate records player team splits. following fictional data uses OHLpkg’s column names: calculations happen plotting. OHLviz retrieve data automatically calculate points-per-game column.
code: skaters <- data.frame(   Name = c("Player A", "Player B", "Player C", "Player D", "Player E"),   Team = c("North", "North", "North", "South", "South"),   GP = c(60, 58, 61, 59, 60),   G = c(35, 28, 31, 40, 22),   A = c(52, 48, 39, 42, 44) )  skaters$PTS <- skaters$G + skaters$A skaters[["Pts/G"]] <- skaters$PTS / skaters$GP

title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: default, plot_scoring_leaders() ranks players PTS.  Change stat select another non-negative numeric column:  Common choices include "PTS", "G", "", "Pts/G". Players ranked highest first. Ties preserve input row order, n limits chart many rows. fewer players available, chart displays available players. rate statistics, choose appropriate qualification threshold plotting:
code: plot_scoring_leaders(   skaters,   n = 5,   title = "Scoring Leaders",   subtitle = "Example player comparison",   caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz" ) plot_scoring_leaders(   skaters,   stat = "G",   n = 3,   title = "Goal Leaders",   caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz" ) qualified_skaters <- skaters[   !is.na(skaters$GP) & skaters$GP >= 60,   ,   drop = FALSE ]  plot_scoring_leaders(   qualified_skaters,   stat = "Pts/G",   title = "Points per Game",   subtitle = "Minimum 60 games played",   caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz" )

title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: plot_team_scoring() displays goals assists stacked bars. Players ranked combined total.  total end bar calculated goals plus assists. function require separate PTS column. data contains exactly one named team, can omit team: Selecting team filters rows. separate traded player’s season totals statistics earned team. Supply team-specific statistics distinction matters. Duplicate player names within selected team produce error. Resolve duplicate records, provide distinct labels two different players share name.
code: plot_team_scoring(   skaters,   team = "North",   title = "North Team Scoring",   caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz" ) north_skaters <- skaters[skaters$Team == "North", ]  plot_team_scoring(north_skaters)

title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: Create fictional goalie dataset: goalie function supports three metrics:  Goalie charts use dots. horizontal axes fitted selected values necessarily start zero. Qualification filters belong upstream. charts rank supplied goalies; automatically apply official league qualification rules.
code: goalies <- data.frame(   Name = c("Goalie A", "Goalie B", "Goalie C", "Goalie D"),   Team = c("North", "South", "East", "West"),   GP = c(42, 45, 38, 40),   GAA = c(2.45, 2.70, 2.30, 3.05),   W = c(25, 30, 22, 18) )  goalies[["SAV%"]] <- c(0.915, 0.908, 0.921, 0.899) plot_goalie_leaders(   goalies,   stat = "GAA",   title = "Goals-Against Average Leaders",   caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz" )

title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: default, save percentage inputs must proportions 0.915.  source uses values 91.5, specify "percent" explicitly: OHLviz guess input units. formats displayed proportions three decimal places. GAA uses two decimal places, wins use whole numbers.
code: plot_goalie_leaders(   goalies,   stat = "SAV%",   title = "Save Percentage Leaders",   caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz" ) percent_goalies <- goalies percent_goalies[["SAV%"]] <- percent_goalies[["SAV%"]] * 100  plot_goalie_leaders(   percent_goalies,   save_pct_scale = "percent" )

title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: OHLviz require data come OHLpkg. scoring leaderboard, specify name statistic columns. Use team_col = NULL team column available:  goalie charts, stat identifies metric determines ranking formatting. stat_col identifies column containing values:
code: custom_skaters <- data.frame(   player = c("Alex", "Sam", "Jordan"),   points = c(65, 72, 58) )  plot_scoring_leaders(   custom_skaters,   stat = "points",   player_col = "player",   team_col = NULL,   title = "Player Points",   caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz" ) custom_goalies <- data.frame(   goalie = c("Alex", "Sam"),   average = c(2.80, 2.20) )  plot_goalie_leaders(   custom_goalies,   stat = "GAA",   stat_col = "average",   player_col = "goalie",   team_col = NULL )

title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: plotting functions support title, subtitle, caption. Scoring goalie leaderboards use colour. Team scoring charts use goals_colour assists_colour. Returned ggplot objects support additional customization:
code: plot_team_scoring(   skaters,   team = "North",   goals_colour = "#142D4E",   assists_colour = "#4FA3D1",   caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz" ) p <- plot_scoring_leaders(skaters)  p +   ggplot2::labs(title = "My Scoring Leaderboard") +   ggplot2::theme(     plot.title = ggplot2::element_text(size = 18)   )

title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: theme_ohl() can also style ggplot2 charts:  Use base_size base_family customize typography. default family "sans" portability. theme controls text, backgrounds, spacing, gridlines. Data colours set separately chart arguments colour scales.
code: ggplot2::ggplot(   skaters,   ggplot2::aes(x = G, y = A) ) +   ggplot2::geom_point(     colour = "#2474B5",     size = 3   ) +   ggplot2::labs(     title = "Goals and Assists",     x = "Goals",     y = "Assists",     caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz"   ) +   theme_ohl()

title: Getting Started with OHLviz
text: Store plot save ggplot2::ggsave(): PDF, change filename extension .pdf. Increase chart height displaying players. Increase width player names, team names, titles need additional room. Inspect exported chart intended display size.
code: p <- plot_scoring_leaders(   skaters,   caption = "Illustrative data | OHLviz" )  ggplot2::ggsave(   filename = "scoring-leaders.png",   plot = p,   width = 10,   height = 7,   units = "in",   dpi = 300,   bg = "white" )

title: OHLviz 0.1.0

title: OHLviz 0.1.0
text: Added plot_scoring_leaders() creating ranked player scoring leaderboards. Supports configurable statistics. Supports configurable leaderboard sizes n. Supports custom player, team, statistic column names. Supports optional team labels. Handles non-finite values validation warnings. Returns standard ggplot object. Added plot_team_scoring() visualizing player scoring within selected team. Displays goals assists stacked bars. Displays combined scoring totals. Supports configurable player limits. Supports custom column names. Supports custom goals assists colours. Allows team argument omitted supplied data contains exactly one team. Added plot_goalie_leaders() ranked goaltender comparisons. Supports save percentage (SAV%). Supports goals-average (GAA). Supports wins (W). Applies statistic-specific ranking direction. Applies statistic-specific value formatting. Supports proportion percentage save-percentage inputs. Supports custom column names. Returns standard ggplot object.
